outcome.technical: Fixes BUG-35-ukq (filed by the orchestrator; no second bug filed, no audit-task.py verb run). plugins/audit/hooks/guard-edits.py: new rule 7. `_is_audit_config(tree)` asks whether the path `_config.tree_for` placed is `<tree root>/_config.CONFIG_REL` - the same root+constant `_config.load` reads, never a literal path - compared over realpath (a symlinked .claude/ is the same file) and by samefile when both exist; it covers the project and a linked worktree of it (tree_for re-roots). `_config_verdict` returns block for `_config.is_subagent(data)`, with a reason naming /audit:panel and a hand edit, and ask for the main session. Wired on the edit-tool path after rule 6 (path decides, so an empty Write is held) and on the MCP path only with a write basis (a read is not held), beside rules 4 and 5. The description said 'rule 6'; the hook already numbers strict manifest state 6 in its code comments, so the new rule is 7, and the module docstring now lists 6 and 7. Dev mode decided and pinned: the rule APPLIES in the plugin's own checkout (cf14/cf15), because rule 3's exception is for plugin source and this file is governance; cf16 pins that rule 3's dev exception still holds. ENUMERATION of edit-tool writers of the config: grep -rn 'audit.config.json' over commands, reference, skills, agents (16 hits), plus a phrasing grep for writing/setting the config: only plugins/audit/commands/init.md instructs a write - section 5 (mirror gitRoot into the config) and step 7.5 (create it with executor.waveWidth auto); both run in the main session, so both now meet an ask, and both now name the prompt in init.md's text (and that a subagent is refused). Every other hit reads the config (worktree.md, report.md, manifest-conventions.md, orchestrator.md, verbs-in-full.md, guide.md, audit-codebase SKILL.md) or describes the panel (panel.md). reference/execute-task.md:593 'edited the config' is about playwright.config.ts, not this file. The panel server writes the config from its own process (scripts/panel/_panel_write.py:1555, temp + os.replace), so no tool hook sees it - confirmed by reading it. SECURITY.md: Known bypass classes item 3 states rule 7, its allow cases, dev mode, and the residual - a shell-form write (sed -i, a redirect, an interpreter) is not refused by any hook and is recorded by the journal only (journal-writes is registered on Bash pre and post, read off hooks.json); the capability-policy section says the same in one paragraph. The fail-mode table row for guard-edits is unchanged: git diff -U0 SECURITY.md holds no table line.
